ev.q: CDC analyzed death data from the National Vital Statistics System
The total estimated lifetime medical and work-loss costs associated with fatal injuries in 2013 was $214 billion.
The mean medical and work-loss cost of any injury death in 2013 was slightly more than $1.1 million
During 2013, the rate of fatal injury was 61.0 per 100,000 population
Males accounted for approximately 78% of these costs and for 67% of injury deaths.
Males accounted for 78% of economic costs ($166.7 billion).
Persons aged 15–44 years accounted for 82% of homicide-associated costs, compared with 65% and 64%
Cost of injury estimates were updated using improved methodology and the most recently available injury data.

methods_quotes.q: Injury death rates were calculated using the U.S. Census Bureau's bridged race population estimates for 2013.
